solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Breaking with courtesy, in France it's a harsh regime

indicators.note: breaking into a word splits it open so that something else can sit inside it

parts.note: acting with courtesy means being polite
the French for 'it is' is c'est

explanation.surface: A diplomat abroad complains that a regime has stopped observing the niceties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' puts CESTA (French c'est plus A) inside POLITE, after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A state run by police surveillance and repression is a classic example of an oppressive government.

clue.text: Make young corporal upset, worried about sappers

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word above it upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Corp is the short form of corporal
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers
to eat at someone is to worry them, so 'worried' can be 'ate'

explanation.surface: A corporal is anxious and upset about the army engineers under him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is taken loosely as a link here: RE (Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers) is followed by ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To procreate is to produce offspring, a plain synonym for making young.

clue.text: Show segment uploaded from al-Jazeera by al-Jazeera

indicators.note: uploaded says the hidden letters are read backwards
segment says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clip from the Al Jazeera news channel is posted online, credited to Al Jazeera itself.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uploaded' turns the run ERABYAL, hidden in 'Jazeera by al', so it reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something bare is to expose or reveal it, an idiom matching 'show' as a verb.

clue.text: British ruler voided community decoration policy

indicators.note: a voided word has had its contents emptied out, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour or decoration
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A local leader honours the community and sets out a policy on awards.
explanation.walkthrough: CYMBELINE is the legendary pre-Roman king of Britain in Shakespeare's play of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline was a legendary king of the ancient Britons, so he is an example of a ruler of Britain.

clue.text: Skip last couple of bits of pulpy, wet seafood

indicators.text: Skip last couple of bits of
indicators.note: skipping the final two letters means they are left off the end

parts.note: squidgy means soft, pulpy and moist

explanation.surface: A diner advises leaving the soggy last few pieces of a seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid is a cephalopod eaten as seafood, often fried as calamari, so it is an example.

clue.text: Sweat from generation spanning working lives

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the outer word reaches round the others

parts.note: a generation is an age
a machine that is working is on
one who lives is

explanation.surface: Working lives across a generation produce a lot of sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat over something informally means to fret or worry about it, which is to agonise.

clue.text: Master with hidden pawn to bring into play

indicators.note: a piece that is hidden has been put out of sight, so it drops out of the word

parts.note: a master of a craft is an expert
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess master conceals a pawn, ready to bring it into the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert force or influence is to apply it, to bring it to bear or put it into play.

clue.text: Sweep often accompanies me, describing chimneys

definitions.meaning: ... and Sweep are a glove-puppet bear and dog from long-running British children's television
chimneys are typically covered in soot, black and grimy

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep talks about his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep' looks like the chimney sweep; it is the puppet dog Sweep, partner of the bear Sooty on British children's TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The puppet bear is Sweep's partner; chimneys are blackened with carbon deposits from smoke.

clue.text: This can copy indiscriminately like a crawler

indicators.note: doing something indiscriminately means at random, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A photocopier that copies anything at all is likened to a fawning hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler is a toady or flatterer, and a sycophantic person behaves in that fawning way.

clue.text: Gold single mother keeps in vault

indicators.note: a word that keeps others holds them inside it

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
sole means single or only

explanation.surface: A lone parent hides her gold in a bank vault.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand tomb, a burial vault housing the dead.

clue.text: Moisture distribution shown by meteorological scales?

definitions.text: Moisture distribution shown by meteorological scales?

parts.words: Moisture distribution shown by meteorological scales?
parts.note: the fish-scale pattern of rippled cloud spread across the heavens, so the scales are those of a fish

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's chart shows how moisture is spread across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' suggests measuring instruments; they are the scales of a fish, which banks of cirrocumulus resemble.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of small fleecy clouds resemble the patterned scales on a mackerel's back, giving the name of this sky.

clue.text: Spray crumbs with common stuffing ingredient

parts.note: crumbs and cor are both British exclamations of surprise
sage, as in sage and onion stuffing

explanation.surface: A cook sprays breadcrumbs mixed with a herb for stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' looks like a verb; it is a small bouquet. COR and 'crumbs' are both mild British exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray of flowers worn on a dress or wrist is the small bouquet called a corsage.

clue.text: Commended about protecting island of those not expecting divine intervention

definitions.text: of those not expecting divine intervention

indicators.note: a word protecting another wraps around it as a shield
about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a soldier cited in dispatches is commended

explanation.surface: Someone praised for shielding an island community from religious meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commended' suggests praise; here it is CITED, as a soldier is cited in dispatches. 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deists believe in a creator who does not intervene in the world, so their views are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Stage reportedly 'owned' by Ms Dunaway?

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word is how something sounds when spoken

parts.note: Faye Dunaway is the American film actress, so something owned by her is Faye's

explanation.surface: A theatre stage said to belong to the actress Faye Dunaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a theatre, fitting the actress; it means a step in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase is one step or period in a process of development, a synonym for stage.

clue.text: One's abstract expressionism's beginning without detail

parts.note: one is, said in the first person, is I'm
an abstract is a summary or precis

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An art critic's note on the origins of abstract expressionism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' looks like art; it is a summary. 'One's' means one is, I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking detail is vague or inexact, which is what imprecise means.

clue.text: In double-bottomed baked goods, dilute concentrated substance

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: pies are baked goods; double-bottomed doubles the last letter, giving piess
to thin a liquid is to dilute it

explanation.surface: Pies with two pastry bases contain a watered-down filling.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom is the last letter, so 'double-bottomed' repeats the S of PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithiness is terseness, the quality of saying much in few words, so it is concentrated substance.

clue.text: Not being educated and not into acing first of exams somehow

indicators.note: one piece put into another goes inside it
somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are reordered
first of means just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: nor means and not

explanation.surface: A student who is not educated yet somehow aces the exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ACING to IGANC; adding E and putting NOR into it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge or learning, the state of not having been educated.

clue.text: Change financial inspection, regularly substituting workers

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, so the change repeats at the next alternate position
substituting means swapping in the workers for a letter of the inspection

parts.note: an audit is an inspection of accounts
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: An accountant changes the audit, regularly bringing in new staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The second and fourth letters of AUDIT, U and I, are each replaced by MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration, as to a law or text, so it is a synonym for change as a noun.

clue.text: Dissembled to cover military actions, lifting rifle

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read from the bottom up
a word set to cover another goes over and around it

parts.note: to dissemble is to deceive, so one who dissembled lied
ops is short for military operations

explanation.surface: A soldier lied to hide operations in which a rifle was stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun; it is a verb, to ransack. 'lifting' reverses LIOPSED as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search and plunder it, and to despoil is likewise to strip it of valuables.

clue.text: Fur one wants on marine mammal

parts.note: mink is a fur

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so letters are missing from the word

explanation.surface: A furrier wants a coat made from a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks: ONE without ON leaves E.
explanation.definitionFit: The minke is a small baleen whale, so it is an example of a sea-dwelling mammal.

clue.text: Bowman's list of options reduced suspicion

parts.note: a menu is a list of options

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a hint is a slight trace or suspicion

explanation.surface: An archer shortens his options because of a suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowman' suggests an archer; Yehudi Menuhin was a violinist, who plays with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Yehudi Menuhin, the celebrated violinist, drew a bow across the strings, a witty sense of the word.

clue.text: Matching kit is a triumph in review of international match

indicators.note: one word in another is placed inside it
a review looks back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
a win is a triumph

explanation.surface: A pundit reviewing an international says matching kit made it a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; a twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper worn together.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a woman's matching cardigan and sweater, worn together as one outfit.

clue.text: In dialect, it's one mode to start with

definitions.text: In dialect, it's one mode to start with

indicators.note: to start with means take the opening letter of each preceding word

explanation.surface: A linguist says dialect begins as one way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a form of expression particular to a people or region, a mode of speech within a dialect.

clue.text: Bunk with a strong smell after time

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other in the answer

parts.note: ripe can mean smelly, as of strong cheese

explanation.surface: A bunk bed that smells strongly after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed; it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk and tripe are both informal words for nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: What gutter removes when crossing road behind pub

indicators.note: behind means this piece comes after the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so this word straddles the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A road gutter carries water away near a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutter' suggests a drain; it is one who guts fish or game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gutting an animal removes its entrails, its internal organs, so the answer is what they take out.

clue.text: Cold wrought iron to reinforce stiff framework

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: to line a garment is to reinforce it

explanation.surface: A blacksmith uses cold wrought iron to strengthen a rigid frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought iron' looks like a material; 'wrought' rearranges IRON to RINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinoline was a stiffened petticoat or hooped frame worn to hold a skirt out.

clue.text: Angel backing the vintage drama

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
Noh is classical Japanese drama

explanation.surface: An investor, or angel, backs an old-fashioned play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel' suggests a theatre backer, fitting 'backing' and 'drama'; it is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel and honey are both affectionate terms for a loved one, like darling.

clue.text: Cafe meal's an unpalatable offence

indicators.note: an unpalatable meal is a bad one, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner complains that a cafe meal is so bad it is criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Malfeasance is wrongdoing, especially by a public official, so it is a type of offence.
